newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TELECOM TECHNICAL TASK TO REGULATE SECTOR.
newsitem.headline: TELECOM TECHNICAL TASK TO REGULATE SECTOR.

text.p: The European Affairs Ministry will send a technical assignment to lead adviser candidates in the Lithuanian Telecom privatisation, an official said.
"The technical assignment is the preparation of the whole privatisation programme," Vytenis Junevichius, director of the privatisation department at the European Affairs Ministry, told Reuters.
"That is, to propose a new regulatory framework for the whole sector, a valuation of Lithuanian Telecom and the strategy of the privatisation deal," Junevichius said.
According to a statement by the euro ministry, replies to the technical assignment are expected in 30 days.
Originally 23 candidates, representing international law firms, consultancies and investment banks, were in the running to act as the government's adviser in the Telecom privatisation.
The government approved a short-list of ten candidates last week.
Junevichius said all of the law firms were cut.
"The adviser will be responsible for closing the deal, for selling the shares," Junevicius said. "That is why we dropped all law firms from the short-list."
Lithuanian Telecom tops a list of 13 key state-owned companies whose privatisation the European affairs ministry is overseeing. The companies are to be sold by open international tenders.
The short-list includes Creditanstalt Investment Bank AG, Merrill Lynch and Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd. Junevichius said there were no leading candidates.
"Creditanstalt has the largest experience in Central and Eastern Europe among all of these," Junevichius said.
"Merrill Lynch has some experience in the privatisation of telecoms in North America," Junevichius said. "And they have been present for quite a long time in Lithuania. They know Lithuania."
"Daiwa is the second largest investment company in the world, in terms of assets, so they have quite a high capacity to sell shares," Junevichius added.
